correctness.rationale: Every de Bruijn circuit is encoded uniquely as one 2-to-2 wiring at each vertex. The shared-(k+1)-mer identity counts two matches per equal wiring. Self-loop avoidance forces the two constant wirings and a four-mer overlap floor. Permutation signs force an even wiring distance and hence overlap divisible by four. For order five a finite exhaustive search checks precisely all 2^14 allowed wirings and 2,096,128 unordered pairs. An independent rooted-edge DFS and actual six-mer intersections reproduced the complete histogram and witness.

value.rationale: A lower bound, congruence, and exact complete pairwise distribution refine a natural biosequence-design impossibility: binary orthogonality cannot be perfect. The count 368 describes every best-possible pair in the first 2048-cycle family, and shows only 23/64 of cycles can participate in a four-overlap pair, always with a unique partner. This is a structurally motivated invariant of a canonical family, not an arbitrary slice or a recomputation of bit-level cross-correlation.
